subject: Food Science
title: Irradiation Controversy
description: Learn Irradiation Controversy in one minute.

hook.text: Food irradiation kills 99.9% of pathogens—including E. coli and Salmonella.

buildup.text: Irradiation exposes food to gamma rays, electron beams, or X-rays. The energy damages bacterial DNA.

discovery.text: Irradiation Controversy reveals the mechanism or argument that changes the picture.

twist.text: Irradiated food isn't radioactive—no more than luggage passing through an airport X-ray scanner.

climax.text: Despite 50+ years of safety data, consumer rejection keeps irradiation marginal.

punchline.text: Proven safe for 50 years. Used by NASA. Rejected by consumers.

quiz.question: Does food irradiation make food radioactive?
options: No—energy passes through the food without being retained, like luggage through an airport X-ray
